record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For every simple graph G on n vertices, does the Nordhaus-Gaddum sum of adjacency spectral radii satisfy lambda_1(G) + lambda_1(G_complement) <= 4n/3 - 5/3 - f(n), where f(n) = (3n - 2 - sqrt(9n^2 - 12n + 12))/6 when n mod 3 = 1, f(n) = 0 when n mod 3 = 2, and f(n) = (3n - 1 - sqrt(9n^2 - 6n + 9))/6 when n mod 3 = 0? If equality holds, must either G or its complement be a complete split graph whose independent set has size ceil(n/3), and also floor(n/3) when n mod 3 = 2?

evidence.quote: Finding an upper bound of Nordhaus-Gaddum type on the index over the class of connected graphs on n vertices, our third problem, was independently posed by Nosal (1970) and by Amin and Hakimi (1972). More than 40 years later, the problem remains open

Conjecture 4.1 (Aouchiche et al. 2008a;Aouchiche and Hansen 2012) For any simple graph G, with complement G, index lambda_1(G) and n vertices we have lambda_1(G) + lambda_1(G) <= 4/3 n - 5/3 - ... This bound is sharp and attained if and only if G or G is a complete split graph with an independent set on ceil(n/3) vertices (and also on floor(n/3) vertices if n mod(3) = 2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph on n vertices and let \bar G denote its complement. Write \lambda_1(H) for the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of the adjacency matrix of a graph H. Define f: \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1} \to \mathbb{R} by
- f(n) = (3n - 2 - \sqrt{9n^2 - 12n + 12})/6 if n \equiv 1 \pmod 3,
- f(n) = 0 if n \equiv 2 \pmod 3,
- f(n) = (3n - 1 - \sqrt{9n^2 - 6n + 9})/6 if n \equiv 0 \pmod 3.

A complete split graph on n vertices with independence number k is the graph on vertex set partitioned as A \sqcup B with |A|=k, |B|=n-k, where A is an independent set, B induces a complete graph K_{n-k}, and every vertex of A is adjacent to every vertex of B.

Prove or disprove the following statements.
(1) For every simple graph G on n \ge 2 vertices,
\lambda_1(G) + \lambda_1(\bar G) \le \tfrac{4n}{3} - \tfrac{5}{3} - f(n).
(2) Equality is attained if and only if G or \bar G is a complete split graph whose independent set has size \lceil n/3 \rceil; and, when n \equiv 2 \pmod 3, equality is also attained if and only if G or \bar G is a complete split graph whose independent set has size \lfloor n/3 \rfloor.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint by Yen-Jen Cheng and Chih-wen Weng ("Nordhaus-Gaddum inequality for the spectral radius of a graph of order n", arXiv:2506.11401) determines the extremal graph maximizing \lambda_1(G)+\lambda_1(\bar G) over all graphs of order n, resolving Stevanović's 2007 conjecture and showing the extremal graph is the complete split graph K_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}\vee \overline{K_{\lceil 2n/3\rceil}}. This identification of extremal graphs yields exactly the bound 4n/3 - 5/3 - f(n) with the stated equality cases, so the Aouchiche-Hansen formulation is resolved.

status_evidence.title: Nordhaus-Gaddum inequality for the spectral radius of a graph of order n
status_evidence.snippet: the extremal graph G of order n that maximizes the sum of the spectral radii of G and its complement... resolves a conjecture posed by Stevanović in 2007
status_evidence.claim: The extremal graph for \lambda_1(G)+\lambda_1(\bar G) is determined, resolving Stevanović's conjecture; the extremal graph is the complete split graph that yields the conjectured Aouchiche-Hansen bound.
